A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Lines of Thought study. Their main text, equations, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison; retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original token-trajectory measurements, dimensionality experiments, stochastic simulations, and untrained-model and gibberish controls in Sections 3–4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a classifier-based analysis of true versus extrapolated token positions in Appendix B.3 and Table 1.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes its stated loop endpoint from 24 to 23. This is a limited pseudocode revision: the surrounding description still specifies 24-position trajectories, and the SVD-based extrapolation and stochastic model remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Walden-derived pseudo-sentences and random-token gibberish. The new separability analysis examines existing true and extrapolated trajectory ensembles, without extending corpus, domain or input-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: The untrained and partially reinitialized GPT-2 controls remain. The Perceptron used for language-versus-gibberish discrimination is also retained. The new SVM is a diagnostic for extrapolation fidelity, not a competing trajectory method or a replacement comparator.

E3.justification: New Appendix B.3 specifies a linear-kernel SVM, a 70/30 training/test split, and classification accuracy for the extrapolation pairs represented in Figure 3. These introduce an additional evaluation protocol; existing experimental settings are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds a quantitative separability check to supplement Figure 3's visual comparison of true and extrapolated positions. Existing dimensionality analysis, gibberish tests, model reinitialization experiments and layer-anomaly analyses remain.

E5.justification: Existing residual-distribution statistics and estimation practices are retained. The new classifier results introduce no repeated-run counts, seed specifications, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds 14 classifier accuracies ranging from 46% to 61%. Earlier plotted results and fitted parameters remain unchanged. Section 3.2 also introduces a trend-description error: it says KL divergence decreases with decreasing K, contrary to the retained Figure 2c.

T1.justification: The extrapolation model, Langevin and Fokker–Planck equations, and Appendix A.2–A.3 derivations are retained. Continuous trajectories already appeared in v1. Replacing U with R in one expression is equivalent notation because R(t) = U(t).

C1.justification: The central manifold and stochastic-model claims remain. The conclusion newly promotes a diagnostic role for the method and potential hybrid architectures, modestly broadening its stated contribution beyond v1's cautious practical outlook.

C2.justification: Section 5 substantially expands the implications: v1 questioned compression usefulness, whereas v3 proposes that individual variability carries meaning and motivates hybrid equation/neural-network architectures, compression and stability through a Neural ODE analogy, and layer diagnostics. Section 3.3 also interprets the new classifier as confirming nonseparability. The explicit limitations paragraph remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds repository access information for trajectory generation, visualization and analysis in the abstract, Methods and references. It also documents the new classifier's kernel and split. Existing trajectory-generation and numerical-integration details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al.'s Neural Ordinary Differential Equations and explicitly relates continuous token dynamics to that framework. It also adds a citation to the authors' code. The remaining literature coverage and physics-inspired positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 receive targeted explanatory rewrites, the implications discussion is expanded, and a new Appendix B.3 shifts subsequent subsection numbering. The overall section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 1, relocates Figure 1 and Algorithm 1, and adjusts figure placement and captions. Appendix Figures 6–15 become A1–A10 with their underlying displays retained. Conference headers and pagination also change.

improvement.justification: The added held-out classifier analysis and code-access information modestly improve quantitative validation and reproducibility over v1. These gains are limited by the unsupported strength of the nonseparability interpretation, the reversed KL-trend sentence, and speculative semantic/compression implications. The core experiments and mathematical development remain unchanged.
